column1: # Campaign 26 source evidence for configured ORDER BY/LIMIT lowering.

column5: ConfiguredOrderedJoinPlan parses once into one typed SELECT, binds the two-relation core once, resolves direct signed-BIGINT FullSchema keys, explicit aliases, and positive projection ordinals, and rejects all other planner shapes; general expression/type resolution, aggregation/window interaction, hints, privilege checks, and optimizer plan construction remain open.

Checked literal LIMIT count, comma offset, and OFFSET syntax lower into one checked ConfiguredLimitWindow; LIMIT 0 returns no join/scan plan before PD or TiKV work. Parameter markers, runtime expression evaluation, unsigned coercion, and general executor/cardinality behavior remain open.

ORDER BY retains source key order and independently maps each DESC bit after binding to stable FullSchema offsets, including unprojected columns and qualified USING-hidden right columns; arbitrary expressions, NULL ordering, collation, generated columns, and physical Sort alternatives remain open.

ORDER BY with explicit checked LIMIT produces the immutable ConfiguredOrderLimitSpec handoff while LIMIT-only remains a distinct structural shape; executor heap, memory quota, spill, partition TopN, distributed TopN, and physical IDs remain open.

The bounded planner deliberately emits no storage TopN or pushdown request and makes its no-pushdown boundary explicit; TiKV/TiFlash pushdown, cop task alternatives, partition behavior, and rule fixpoint semantics remain open.

The configured path carries resolved ordering metadata to its future executor consumer without selecting a general physical Sort/TopN implementation; property matching, enforced properties, cost comparisons, and alternative implementation enumeration remain open.
